source.title: Quantifying Generalization in Reinforcement Learning
source.venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 97

confidence_rationale: This is the closest domain match to MECH-472's substrate: a reward-driven agent whose competence is measured on procedurally generated CONTEXTS (levels), with training and test sets held strictly disjoint. The paper's central empirical result -- that agents overfit even to large training sets and that same-environment evaluation systematically overstates competence -- is exactly the mechanism MECH-472 asserts. High source_quality (canonical, widely replicated benchmark from a strong group) and high mapping_fidelity (RL agent, held-out CONTEXT, not merely held-out samples); the only discount is that CoinRun measures generalization at test time rather than gating a PROMOTION-to-durable decision, which is REE's specific framing.
failure_signatures: An agent can reach near-ceiling reward on its training levels while performing substantially worse on held-out levels drawn from the same generator -- so training-context success is not evidence of acquired skill.

Overfitting persists up into training sets of thousands of distinct levels, so a small held-out gap is only obtained with very large context diversity; a modest number of training contexts guarantees the gap MECH-472 is trying to detect.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Using the same environments for training and testing gives little insight into an agent's ability to generalize; with procedurally generated environments split into disjoint train/test sets, agents overfit to surprisingly large training sets, and the train-vs-test performance gap is the honest measure of generalization.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-472 asserts that a competence update should be promoted to durable only on evidence from contexts that did NOT generate it. Cobbe et al. operationalise precisely this: the held-out level set is the 'context that did not generate the competence', and the observed train-minus-test gap is the memorisation-vs-acquisition signal MECH-472 proposes to threshold on.
mapping.mapping_caveat: CoinRun evaluates generalization as a reporting metric at the end of training; it does not gate a promotion decision or distinguish 'durable' from 'provisional' competence stores, which is the specific control-plane action MECH-472 adds. The transfer is from 'held-out evaluation reveals memorisation' (well supported) to 'therefore gate promotion on held-out evidence' (a design inference REE must still justify on its own substrate).
mapping.source_context: Deep RL (PPO) on the CoinRun / procedurally generated platformer benchmark; simulated 2D game levels, no biological or human data.

confidence_components.notes: Transfer risk is low because REE's own agents are RL-like and evaluated over contexts, so the animal->human / task->REE gap that discounts many neuroscience pulls does not apply here. The residual risk is framing, not domain: measurement vs promotion-gating.
